open_questions.question: Does the full coupled Schrodinger (electrons) + Landau-Lifshitz (spins) time integrator reproduce the collapse snapshots of Fig. 2 (t = 5912-5960 t0) and the collapse time t* ~ lambda/(s0 a)?
open_questions.why_heavy: Requires building the self-consistent quantum-classical solver: tight-binding Schrodinger stepping on the lattice, feeding the electron spin density s into the LL equation each timestep, integrated over ~6000 t0. This is the actual dynamics the static+scaling core only brackets.
open_questions.compute_estimate: Medium-heavy: L~128-256 lattice, ~6000 time steps, per-step dense/sparse eig or Chebyshev propagation of the electron Hamiltonian. nuc13 CPU or uicgpu for the electron diagonalization.
open_questions.next_step: Implement the coupled stepper (Crank-Nicolson or Chebyshev for Schrodinger; Heun/RK4 for LL with the STT torque term), seed with the relaxed BP skyrmion, measure t* vs lambda and compare the ~5900 t0 figure.

open_questions.question: Is the topological-charge collapse Q(t): 1 -> 0 correlated with the nucleation of an intense electron b-field vortex carrying its own topological charge, as claimed in Sec. III (lines 304-330, 520)?
open_questions.why_heavy: The b-field is a topological density built from the electron spin field s (not the localized S); it only exists once the electron dynamics is solved self-consistently. Needs the full solver of Q1 plus a Berg-Luscher charge computed on the electron spin texture s.
open_questions.compute_estimate: Same solver as Q1 plus per-step lattice charge of s; negligible extra cost once the solver exists.
open_questions.next_step: After Q1, compute Q_S(t) and Q_b(t) = Berg-Luscher charge of s(r,t); test the anti-correlation / conservation-transfer claim at the collapse instant.

open_questions.question: How does the exchange-dissipation term d smooth the skyrmion->ferromagnet transition, and what is the quantitative d-dependence of the Q(t) curves in Fig. 3?
open_questions.why_heavy: Requires the LL equation with the added exchange-dissipation term over a scan of d, each a full coupled run; the paper shows a family of Q(t) curves parameterized by dissipation.
open_questions.compute_estimate: N_d full coupled runs (Q1 solver) for d in a scan; linear in number of dissipation values.
open_questions.next_step: Add the exchange-dissipation operator to the LL RHS, run a d-scan, reproduce the smoothing trend and the dissipation-dependent transition sharpness of Fig. 3.

open_questions.question: Does the exact self-similar solution (Eqs. 24-25) of the driven LL equation quantitatively match the collapsing core profile f(X) from the full numerical run, beyond the exponent (alpha,beta) match?
open_questions.why_heavy: We verified the EXPONENTS by dimensional balance; verifying the full self-similar PROFILE f(X) requires (a) solving the self-similar ODE for f, and (b) extracting the rescaled core profile from the numerical collapse and collapsing the curves onto one master profile.
open_questions.compute_estimate: Light for the ODE (1-D boundary value problem); the profile extraction needs the Q1 solver output.
open_questions.next_step: Solve the self-similar ODE (Eq. ~22-23) for f(X) with the stated boundary conditions; overlay rescaled numerical cores from Q1 to test data collapse.

open_questions.question: How sensitive is the collapse (existence of a finite-time singularity vs. a smooth crossover) to lattice cutoff a, initial size lambda_0, current polarization Bp, and electron density ne?
open_questions.why_heavy: A parameter-space study of the singularity: whether t* stays finite and the beta=1/2 scaling holds across (a, lambda_0, Bp, ne). Each point is a full coupled run; the phase boundary between singular collapse and dissipation-smoothed crossover is the deliverable.
open_questions.compute_estimate: Heavy: multi-dimensional sweep of full coupled runs; embarrassingly parallel -> ALCF Crux or a subagent fan-out.
open_questions.next_step: Grid (lambda_0, Bp, ne) at fixed a, run the Q1 solver at each, fit beta and t*, and map where the self-similar collapse survives vs. where dissipation dominates.
